title: Model version retirement runbook and compatibility plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define an operational runbook and customer-facing plan for retiring legacy model versions while preserving customer continuity through version pinning, automated migration helpers, and published performance profiles. This ticket coordinates PM, runtime, SDK, and docs work to ensure predictable rollouts, clear notices, and measurable quality preservation when older model versions are deprecated.

Scope: retirement lifecycle for model versions in the Redwood model catalog (hosted and dedicated). Includes: announcement cadence, pinning semantics and tooling, migration guides, compatibility tests, performance-profile publishing, dashboarding for impact, and rollback/fallback policy. Excludes on-prem air-gapped incident playbooks (will be a follow-up ticket).

Deliverables:
- Internal runbook (this ticket) covering stages, owners, and success criteria.
- Public notice templates and migration guide for customers.
- CLI/SDK helper (migration-checker) to identify pins and incompatible usages.
- Automated dashboard: pre/post migration quality and cost delta by customer cohort.
- Code: server-side deprecation flags + gradual traffic gating feature.
- Post-mortem template and lessons learned checklist for each retirement.

Success criteria: No more than 2% of active customers experience >1.5x regression in latency or token cost after migration; 95% of pinned users have a documented migration path within the first 30 days of announcement; no critical customer incidents attributable to missing communications or incompatible API behavior during retirements.

public_notice_templates: Initial notice (60 days): We are planning to retire model version {version} on {retire_date}. Recommended action: pin to a compatible version or follow the migration guide at {link}. If you have contractual requirements, contact support.

Final notice (7 days): Reminder: model version {version} will be retired in 7 days. If your code pins this version, please update to {recommended_version} or enable automatic fallback. See {migration_link} for instructions.

Critical deprecation (3 days): Deprecated model {version} will be removed in 72 hours. Requests pinning the version will be redirected to {fallback_version} with a deprecation warning header. Contact Customer Success immediately if you need more time.
migration_guide_outline: 1) Inventory pins: use migration-checker CLI (redwood-cli migrate --check) to list customers and routes using {version}
2) Test replacement: recommended_model = {recommended_version}; run sampling evals provided in /evals/{version}-migration to verify output parity
3) Update SDK: change model parameter or use pin override policy in client config
4) Use staged rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on degradation thresholds
5) Validate in Console: confirm latency and token-cost deltas are within expected bounds
6) After migration: mark customer as migrated in CRM and remove pin entry
runtime_changes: Add 'deprecated_until' and 'deprecated_reason' fields to model metadata in catalog
Return deprecation warning header 'X-Model-Deprecation' on calls to deprecated versions when feature flag enabled
Implement traffic gating: allow percentage-based routing away from deprecated variants
Provide automatic fallback mapping for pinned requests when safe replacement exists
compatibility_tests: Automated unit tests comparing top-k tokens and sampling distribution between old and recommended model across canonical prompts
Integration smoke tests for SDKs ensuring no schema/parameter breaking changes
Quality eval: run existing eval suites and threshold checks (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding cosine similarity/eval harness score change < 5%)
Performance delta tests for median latency and p95 tokens/sec
migration_metrics_dashboard_spec: Cohorts: pinned vs unpinned customers; Hosted vs Dedicated; high-QPS vs low-QPS
Metrics: token cost delta, median latency, p95 latency, eval score delta, error rate, rollback events
Alerts: >5% cohort customers with eval score regression >5% or >10% increase in token cost
Reporting cadence: daily during announcement window, hourly during final 7 days
open_decisions: Default notice duration: legal prefers 60 days for hosted; confirm if we standardize 90 days for major-model breaks
Pin semantics for Dedicated customers: should we allow automatic fallback by default or require explicit opt-in?
Migration-checker UX: expose in Console or keep CLI-only for first iteration?
Rollback policy: define clear SLA for automatic rollback on observed regressions vs manual rollback by customer
